synthesis: The source tests complementary consequences of the proposed log-correlated freezing picture: fixed-window maxima probe the three-halves centering and predicted extreme-value distribution, while the partition-function construction turns fixed-window zeta values into a beta-indexed free-energy curve whose change at beta=1 probes the freezing plateau.
source_support: Unit openalex_w1986417812_v2_u06 reports that the mean maximum is substantially closer to the c=3/2 normalization than to c=1/2; unit openalex_w1986417812_v2_u07 compares the centered maximum distribution and left tail with the log-correlated prediction while stating that the agreement is inconclusive; unit openalex_w1986417812_v2_u08 defines the zeta partition function and reports renormalized free energy consistent with beta+1/beta below beta=1 and a plateau near 2 above it.
nonparaphrase_operation: It connects two different levels of observation—extreme-value location and shape versus an aggregate beta-response curve—and identifies them as distinct tests of the same proposed picture, so agreement in one observable does not substitute for agreement in the other.
limits: The evidence is finite-height and protocol-dependent, the maximum distribution converges slowly, lower-order arithmetic corrections are omitted from one comparison and externally subtracted in the free-energy comparison, and two-column extraction obscures some formulas and plot details; none of the numerical agreements establishes a zeta extreme-value law or freezing transition.
quality_reason: Accepted because three distinct parent units jointly support a concrete complementarity between maximum-based discrimination and a partition-function freezing test that no parent supplies alone, with the source's epistemic and representation limits retained.
